questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Particulate Nature of Matter and State Changes
questions.Question: Which of the following phenomena provides direct experimental evidence that matter is particulate and in continuous random motion?
questions.Explanation: Brownian motion (observed in pollen grains or smoke particles) and diffusion of gases/liquids prove that matter consists of particles in continuous random motion.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Particulate Nature of Matter and State Changes
questions.Question: The physical change in which a substance transitions directly from solid to gas without passing through the liquid phase is called
questions.Explanation: Sublimation is the direct phase change from solid to gas upon heating (e.g., iodine crystals, ammonium chloride, naphthalene, dry ice).

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Particulate Nature of Matter and State Changes
questions.Question: Which of the following compounds readily sublimes on heating?
questions.Explanation: Solid ammonium chloride, iodine, and dry ice (solid CO2) sublime upon heating, bypassing the liquid state.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Particulate Nature of Matter and State Changes
questions.Question: According to the kinetic theory of matter, what happens to the average kinetic energy of gas molecules when temperature increases?
questions.OptionB: It remains constant regardless of temperature
questions.OptionC: It fluctuates unpredictably without following any law
questions.OptionD: It increases proportionally with absolute temperature (in Kelvin)
questions.Option_b: It remains constant regardless of temperature
questions.Option_c: It fluctuates unpredictably without following any law
questions.Option_d: It increases proportionally with absolute temperature (in Kelvin)
questions.Explanation: Kinetic theory establishes that average kinetic energy is directly proportional to absolute temperature (E_k = 3/2 kT).

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Particulate Nature of Matter and State Changes
questions.Question: Which state of matter has a definite volume but takes the shape of its containing vessel?
questions.Explanation: Liquids have fixed volumes due to intermolecular forces, but their particles can slide over one another, taking the shape of the container.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Particulate Nature of Matter and State Changes
questions.Question: A pure crystalline solid substance has a sharp, well-defined melting point because its particles
questions.OptionA: are free to move about like gas molecules
questions.OptionB: are arranged in a regular, orderly three-dimensional crystal lattice with uniform bond strengths
questions.OptionC: repel each other through powerful nuclear forces
questions.OptionD: possess zero kinetic energy at room temperature
questions.Option_a: are free to move about like gas molecules
questions.Option_b: are arranged in a regular, orderly three-dimensional crystal lattice with uniform bond strengths
questions.Option_c: repel each other through powerful nuclear forces
questions.Option_d: possess zero kinetic energy at room temperature
questions.Explanation: Pure crystalline solids have a sharp melting point because identical intermolecular or ionic bonds require the exact same thermal energy to break.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Particulate Nature of Matter and State Changes
questions.Question: Evaporation differs from boiling because evaporation
questions.OptionA: takes place throughout the entire bulk of the liquid only at a fixed temperature
questions.OptionB: produces bubbles of steam within the liquid
questions.OptionC: occurs only at the surface of the liquid and at any temperature below the boiling point
questions.Option_a: takes place throughout the entire bulk of the liquid only at a fixed temperature
questions.Option_b: produces bubbles of steam within the liquid
questions.Option_c: occurs only at the surface of the liquid and at any temperature below the boiling point
questions.Explanation: Evaporation is a surface phenomenon occurring at any temperature, whereas boiling occurs throughout the liquid at a specific temperature where vapour pressure equals external pressure.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Particulate Nature of Matter and State Changes
questions.Question: Why does evaporation cause cooling of the remaining liquid?
questions.OptionA: Water molecules destroy heat photons during phase change
questions.OptionB: The liquid absorbs cold atmospheric nitrogen gas
questions.OptionC: Condensation produces an exothermic cooling effect
questions.OptionD: High-energy molecules escape from the surface, lowering the average kinetic energy of the remaining molecules
questions.Option_a: Water molecules destroy heat photons during phase change
questions.Option_b: The liquid absorbs cold atmospheric nitrogen gas
questions.Option_c: Condensation produces an exothermic cooling effect
questions.Option_d: High-energy molecules escape from the surface, lowering the average kinetic energy of the remaining molecules
questions.Explanation: Only the most energetic molecules overcome intermolecular forces and escape; the remaining liquid has lower mean kinetic energy, hence lower temperature.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Particulate Nature of Matter and State Changes
questions.Question: The boiling point of a liquid is reached when its
questions.OptionA: saturated vapour pressure equals the external atmospheric pressure
questions.OptionC: density becomes greater than that of solid ice
questions.OptionD: colour changes from transparent to milky white
questions.Option_a: saturated vapour pressure equals the external atmospheric pressure
questions.Option_c: density becomes greater than that of solid ice
questions.Option_d: colour changes from transparent to milky white
questions.Explanation: Boiling occurs when the liquid's saturated vapour pressure equals external atmospheric pressure, allowing vapour bubbles to form inside the liquid.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Particulate Nature of Matter and State Changes
questions.Question: On top of Mount Everest where atmospheric pressure is low, water boils at
questions.Explanation: Lower atmospheric pressure means water's vapour pressure reaches atmospheric pressure at a lower temperature (~70°C on Everest).

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Particulate Nature of Matter and State Changes
questions.Question: Which of the following represents a chemical change rather than a physical change?
questions.OptionC: Rusting of iron in moist air
questions.Option_c: Rusting of iron in moist air
questions.Explanation: Rusting forms a new substance (hydrated iron(III) oxide, Fe2O3·xH2O) with new chemical bonds, which is irreversible by simple physical means.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Particulate Nature of Matter and State Changes
questions.Question: A mixture of kerosene and water can be separated in the laboratory using a
questions.Explanation: Kerosene and water are immiscible liquids of different densities; a separating funnel allows the denser bottom aqueous layer to be tapped off.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Particulate Nature of Matter and State Changes
questions.Question: Which separation technique is most suitable for separating a mixture of pigments in green spinach leaves?
questions.Explanation: Chromatography separates solutes based on their differential partitioning between a stationary phase (paper) and mobile solvent phase.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Particulate Nature of Matter and State Changes
questions.Question: Fractional distillation is used to separate miscible liquids that have
questions.Explanation: Fractional distillation separates miscible liquids (e.g., ethanol/water, petroleum fractions) based on differences in boiling points using a fractionating column.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Particulate Nature of Matter and State Changes
questions.Question: The temperature during the melting of a pure substance remains constant until all the solid turns into liquid because the heat supplied is used to
questions.OptionA: increase the speed of electron orbitals
questions.OptionC: overcome intermolecular forces of attraction (latent heat of fusion)
questions.OptionD: radiate infrared waves into the container
questions.Option_a: increase the speed of electron orbitals
questions.Option_c: overcome intermolecular forces of attraction (latent heat of fusion)
questions.Option_d: radiate infrared waves into the container
questions.Explanation: During a phase change, heat input (latent heat) breaks intermolecular lattice bonds rather than raising temperature, keeping temperature constant.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Atomic Structure, Isotopes, and Electronic Configuration
questions.Question: An atom of an element is electrically neutral because the number of
questions.OptionA: neutrons equals the number of protons
questions.OptionD: protons in the nucleus equals the number of electrons orbiting the nucleus
questions.Option_a: neutrons equals the number of protons
questions.Option_d: protons in the nucleus equals the number of electrons orbiting the nucleus
questions.Explanation: Protons have a +1 charge and electrons have a -1 charge; equal numbers produce zero net charge.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Atomic Structure, Isotopes, and Electronic Configuration
questions.Question: The atomic number (Z) of an atom represents the total number of
questions.OptionD: valence electrons in the outermost shell
questions.Option_d: valence electrons in the outermost shell
questions.Explanation: Atomic number Z is the number of protons in an atom's nucleus, uniquely defining the chemical identity of the element.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Atomic Structure, Isotopes, and Electronic Configuration
questions.Question: The mass number (A) of an atom is defined as the sum of
questions.OptionB: protons and neutrons (nucleons) in the nucleus
questions.Option_b: protons and neutrons (nucleons) in the nucleus
questions.Explanation: Mass number A = number of protons (Z) + number of neutrons (N).

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Atomic Structure, Isotopes, and Electronic Configuration
questions.Question: An atom has a mass number of 35 and an atomic number of 17. How many neutrons are in its nucleus?
questions.Explanation: Neutrons = Mass Number (A) - Atomic Number (Z) = 35 - 17 = 18 neutrons.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Atomic Structure, Isotopes, and Electronic Configuration
questions.Question: Isotopes of the same chemical element have the same
questions.OptionA: mass number but different atomic numbers
questions.OptionB: number of neutrons but different number of protons
questions.OptionD: atomic number (protons) but different mass numbers (neutrons)
questions.Option_a: mass number but different atomic numbers
questions.Option_b: number of neutrons but different number of protons
questions.Option_d: atomic number (protons) but different mass numbers (neutrons)
questions.Explanation: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with identical proton numbers (Z) but differing neutron numbers (N), leading to different mass numbers (A).

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Atomic Structure, Isotopes, and Electronic Configuration
questions.Question: Chlorine exists as two isotopes: Cl-35 (75% abundance) and Cl-37 (25% abundance). What is the relative atomic mass of chlorine?

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Atomic Structure, Isotopes, and Electronic Configuration
questions.Question: What is the electronic configuration of a sodium atom (Na, atomic number 11) in the ground state?
questions.Explanation: Sodium has 11 electrons: 1s² (2) + 2s² 2p⁶ (8) + 3s¹ (1) = 11 electrons.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Atomic Structure, Isotopes, and Electronic Configuration
questions.Question: According to the Aufbau principle, electrons fill atomic orbitals in order of
questions.Explanation: Aufbau principle states that in the ground state, electrons occupy orbitals of lowest energy first (e.g., 1s < 2s < 2p < 3s < 3p < 4s < 3d).

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Atomic Structure, Isotopes, and Electronic Configuration
questions.Question: Hund's Rule of Maximum Multiplicity states that when filling degenerate orbitals,
questions.OptionA: no two electrons can have identical four quantum numbers
questions.OptionB: electrons must fill the 3d subshell before the 4s subshell
questions.OptionC: orbitals can hold a maximum of four electrons
questions.OptionD: electrons occupy singly with parallel spins before pairing occurs
questions.Option_a: no two electrons can have identical four quantum numbers
questions.Option_b: electrons must fill the 3d subshell before the 4s subshell
questions.Option_c: orbitals can hold a maximum of four electrons
questions.Option_d: electrons occupy singly with parallel spins before pairing occurs
questions.Explanation: Hund's rule dictates that electrons singly occupy each degenerate orbital in a subshell before pairing to minimize electron-electron repulsion.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Atomic Structure, Isotopes, and Electronic Configuration
questions.Question: Pauli's Exclusion Principle states that no two electrons in an atom can have the same
questions.Explanation: Pauli's exclusion principle implies that an orbital holds at most two electrons, and they must have opposite spins (ms = +1/2 and -1/2).

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Atomic Structure, Isotopes, and Electronic Configuration
questions.Question: The maximum number of electrons that can be accommodated in a principal energy level (shell) with quantum number n is given by
questions.Explanation: The maximum electron capacity of shell n is 2n² (n=1 holds 2, n=2 holds 8, n=3 holds 18, n=4 holds 32).

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Atomic Structure, Isotopes, and Electronic Configuration
questions.Question: How many unpaired electrons are present in a neutral nitrogen atom (atomic number 7) in its ground state?
questions.Explanation: Nitrogen has configuration 1s² 2s² 2px¹ 2py¹ 2pz¹. The three 2p orbitals each hold one unpaired electron.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Atomic Structure, Isotopes, and Electronic Configuration
questions.Question: Which of the following transition metal atoms exhibits an anomalous ground-state electron configuration with a half-filled 3d subshell?
questions.Explanation: Chromium has configuration [Ar] 4s¹ 3d⁵ rather than 4s² 3d⁴ because a half-filled 3d⁵ subshell confers enhanced stability due to exchange energy.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Atomic Structure, Isotopes, and Electronic Configuration
questions.Question: What species is formed when an atom of magnesium (Z=12) loses two valence electrons?
questions.Explanation: Magnesium loses its two 3s valence electrons to form a dipositive cation Mg²⁺ with stable neon noble-gas configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁶.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Atomic Structure, Isotopes, and Electronic Configuration
questions.Question: Radioactive isotopes (radioisotopes) such as Carbon-14 are widely used in archaeology for
questions.OptionB: radiocarbon dating of ancient organic materials
questions.Option_b: radiocarbon dating of ancient organic materials
questions.Explanation: Carbon-14 (half-life ~5730 years) decays by beta emission and is used to date biological artifacts up to ~50,000 years old.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: The Periodic Table and Periodic Properties
questions.Question: In the modern Periodic Table, elements are arranged in order of increasing
questions.Explanation: Moseley showed that arranging elements by increasing atomic number (Z) resolves anomalies of Mendeleev's mass-based table.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: The Periodic Table and Periodic Properties
questions.Question: Elements in the same vertical column (group) of the Periodic Table have similar chemical properties because they have the same
questions.OptionD: number of valence electrons in their outermost shell
questions.Option_d: number of valence electrons in their outermost shell
questions.Explanation: Chemical reactivity is determined by valence electrons; elements in the same group possess identical valence electron configurations.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: The Periodic Table and Periodic Properties
questions.Question: Across a period from left to right in the Periodic Table, the atomic radius generally
questions.OptionA: decreases due to increasing effective nuclear charge pulling electrons closer
questions.OptionB: increases because more shells are added
questions.Option_a: decreases due to increasing effective nuclear charge pulling electrons closer
questions.Option_b: increases because more shells are added
questions.Explanation: Across a period, protons increase while electrons enter the same shell; the increased effective nuclear charge pulls electrons tighter, shrinking atomic radius.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: The Periodic Table and Periodic Properties
questions.Question: Down a group from top to bottom in the Periodic Table, atomic radius increases because
questions.OptionB: an additional electron shell is added at each successive period
questions.Option_b: an additional electron shell is added at each successive period
questions.Explanation: Each step down a group adds a principal energy level (shell), increasing electron screening and expanding atomic size.

questions.Subject: Chemistry

questions.Question: First ionization energy is defined as the energy required to remove

questions.OptionB: all valence electrons simultaneously in aqueous solution

questions.OptionD: one proton from the nucleus of a radioactive element

questions.Topic: The Periodic Table and Periodic Properties

questions.Option_c: metallic character increases across the period

questions.OptionC: release energy when gaining an electron in the gas phase
questions.OptionD: conduct an electric current in the molten state

questions.Option_d: conduct an electric current in the molten state
questions.Explanation: Pauling defined electronegativity as the relative power of an atom in a chemical bond to attract shared electron density toward itself.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: The Periodic Table and Periodic Properties
questions.Question: Which of the following elements has the highest electronegativity value on the Pauling scale?
questions.Explanation: Fluorine is the most electronegative element (value 4.0), having a small atomic radius and high effective nuclear charge.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: The Periodic Table and Periodic Properties
questions.Question: Noble gases (Group 18) are chemically inert under normal conditions because they possess

questions.OptionC: zero protons in their atomic nuclei

questions.Option_b: an odd number of valence electrons
questions.Option_c: zero protons in their atomic nuclei
questions.Explanation: Noble gases have fully filled valence shells, giving exceptional thermodynamic stability and near-zero affinity to gain or lose electrons.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: The Periodic Table and Periodic Properties
questions.Question: Which block of the Periodic Table contains the transition metals characterized by partially filled d-orbitals?
questions.Explanation: Transition metals occupy Groups 3 to 12 (the d-block), exhibiting variable oxidation states, coloured ions, and catalytic properties.

questions.Subject: Chemistry

questions.Explanation: First electron affinity: X(g) + e⁻ → X⁻(g), typically exothermic for non-metals gaining an electron.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: The Periodic Table and Periodic Properties
questions.Question: Which of the following elements displays amphoteric behavior, reacting with both acids and strong alkalis?
questions.Explanation: Aluminium and zinc form amphoteric oxides and hydroxides (e.g., Al2O3 reacts with HCl to give AlCl3 and with NaOH to give aluminate [Al(OH)4]⁻).

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: The Periodic Table and Periodic Properties
questions.Question: Down Group 1 (the alkali metals), chemical reactivity with water

questions.Option_b: decreases down the group as density rises
questions.Option_c: remains identical from lithium to francium
questions.Explanation: Down Group 1, valence electrons are further from the nucleus and shielded, reducing ionization energy and making outer electrons easier to lose.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Which of the following pairs of elements will form an electrovalent (ionic) compound?
questions.Explanation: Sodium (Group 1 metal) transfers its 3s¹ electron to chlorine (Group 17 non-metal), forming an ionic lattice of Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Which of the following ions contains a coordinate (dative covalent) bond?
questions.Explanation: In NH4⁺, the lone pair on ammonia (:NH3) is donated to a hydrogen ion (H⁺), creating a coordinate covalent N→H bond.

questions.Explanation: In NH4Cl, nitrogen and hydrogen are joined by covalent (including coordinate) bonds within NH4⁺, which forms an ionic bond with Cl⁻.

questions.Subject: Chemistry

questions.Explanation: Homonuclear diatomic molecules like Cl-Cl share bonding electrons equally because both atoms have identical electronegativities (ΔEN = 0).

questions.Subject: Chemistry

questions.Explanation: Kw = [H⁺][OH⁻] = 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴ at 25°C. In pure water, [H⁺] = [OH⁻] = 1.0 × 10⁻⁷ mol/dm³, so pH = 7.0.

questions.Subject: Chemistry

questions.Subject: Chemistry

questions.Explanation: In K4[Fe(CN)6], the [Fe(CN)6]⁴⁻ complex ion remains intact in aqueous solution rather than dissociating into free Fe²⁺ and CN⁻ ions.

questions.Subject: Chemistry

questions.Question: Which of the following nitrates decomposes on heating to yield a metal oxide, brown nitrogen dioxide gas, and oxygen gas?

questions.Explanation: Zinc is oxidized from 0 to +2 by losing 2 electrons, thereby causing the reduction of Cu²⁺ to Cu; hence Zn is the reducing agent.

questions.Explanation: Cr2O7²⁻ (orange, Cr +6) is reduced by reducing agents (like SO2 or ethanol) to Cr³⁺ (green, Cr +3).

questions.Subject: Chemistry

questions.Subject: Chemistry

questions.Explanation: Discharging 1 mole of O2 requires 4 Faradays (4OH⁻ → 2H2O + O2 + 4e⁻). Moles of O2 = 0.4 / 4 = 0.1 mol. Volume = 0.1 × 22.4 dm³ = 2.24 dm³.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: In the laboratory preparation of hydrogen gas, granulated zinc is reacted with dilute hydrochloric acid. Why is concentrated nitric acid unsuitable for this preparation?
questions.OptionA: Nitric acid is a powerful oxidizing agent that oxidizes the liberated hydrogen to water rather than releasing hydrogen gas
questions.OptionB: Nitric acid does not react with zinc metal
questions.OptionC: Zinc dissolves in nitric acid without forming any salt
questions.OptionD: The reaction produces toxic chlorine gas instead
questions.Option_a: Nitric acid is a powerful oxidizing agent that oxidizes the liberated hydrogen to water rather than releasing hydrogen gas
questions.Option_b: Nitric acid does not react with zinc metal
questions.Option_c: Zinc dissolves in nitric acid without forming any salt
questions.Option_d: The reaction produces toxic chlorine gas instead
questions.Explanation: HNO3 oxidizes nascent hydrogen immediately to H2O, yielding nitrogen oxides (NO, NO2) instead of H2 gas.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Which of the following drying agents is most suitable for drying hydrogen gas in the laboratory?
questions.Explanation: Anhydrous CaCl2 pellets in a U-tube absorb moisture without reacting with neutral hydrogen gas.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: The three natural isotopes of hydrogen are known as
questions.Explanation: Protium (1 proton, 0 neutrons), deuterium (heavy hydrogen, 1 proton, 1 neutron), and radioactive tritium (1 proton, 2 neutrons) are hydrogen's isotopes.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Water gas, an important industrial fuel, is a gaseous mixture of
questions.Explanation: Passing steam over red-hot coke (C + H2O → CO + H2) produces water gas (synthesis gas).

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: In the laboratory preparation of oxygen gas, which catalyst is added to accelerate the thermal decomposition of potassium chlorate (KClO3)?
questions.Explanation: 2KClO3(s) → 2KCl(s) + 3O2(g), catalyzed by MnO2 which lowers the decomposition temperature from 400°C to 250°C.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: A glowing wooden splint rekindles (bursts into flame) in the presence of which gas?
questions.Explanation: The confirmatory test for oxygen is its ability to rekindle a glowing wooden splint due to its combustion-supporting property.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Allotropy is the existence of an element in two or more different physical forms in the same state. The two allotropes of oxygen are
questions.Explanation: Oxygen exhibits allotropy as diatomic oxygen (O2) and triatomic ozone (O3), an allotrope that absorbs harmful solar UV rays.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Hardness of water is caused by the presence of dissolved
questions.OptionA: sodium and potassium ions (Na⁺ and K⁺)
questions.OptionD: calcium and magnesium ions (Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺)
questions.Option_a: sodium and potassium ions (Na⁺ and K⁺)
questions.Option_d: calcium and magnesium ions (Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺)
questions.Explanation: Hard water fails to lather readily with soap because Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ precipitate insoluble scum (calcium stearate).

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Temporary hardness of water is caused by dissolved calcium hydrogen carbonate, Ca(HCO3)2. It can be removed by
questions.OptionD: bubbling carbon dioxide through the water
questions.Option_d: bubbling carbon dioxide through the water
questions.Explanation: Boiling decomposes soluble Ca(HCO3)2 into insoluble CaCO3 precipitate (kettle fur), eliminating temporary hardness: Ca(HCO3)2 → CaCO3↓ + H2O + CO2.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Permanent hardness of water is caused by dissolved calcium and magnesium sulphates and chlorides. It can be removed chemically by adding
questions.Explanation: Na2CO3 precipitates the offending ions as insoluble carbonates: CaSO4(aq) + Na2CO3(aq) → CaCO3(s)↓ + Na2SO4(aq).

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Modern water softening in domestic and industrial boilers is carried out using an ion-exchange resin (Permutit), which replaces
questions.OptionA: H⁺ ions with toxic heavy metal ions
questions.OptionC: Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions with harmless Na⁺ ions
questions.Option_a: H⁺ ions with toxic heavy metal ions
questions.Option_c: Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions with harmless Na⁺ ions
questions.Explanation: Cation-exchange resins bind divalent Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions from hard water and release non-interfering Na⁺ ions.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: An advantage of hard water over soft water is that hard water
questions.OptionA: lathers instantly with very little soap
questions.OptionB: prevents furring in electric kettles and industrial boilers
questions.OptionC: is completely free of dissolved mineral ions
questions.OptionD: contains calcium ions essential for healthy bones and teeth, and does not dissolve lead from old pipes
questions.Option_a: lathers instantly with very little soap
questions.Option_b: prevents furring in electric kettles and industrial boilers
questions.Option_c: is completely free of dissolved mineral ions
questions.Option_d: contains calcium ions essential for healthy bones and teeth, and does not dissolve lead from old pipes
questions.Explanation: Hard water provides dietary calcium and deposits a protective coating of CaCO3 in pipes that prevents toxic lead poisoning.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Heavy water (D2O) contains deuterium (²H) instead of protium. It is utilized in nuclear fission reactors as a
questions.Explanation: Heavy water slows down fast fission neutrons without capturing them, facilitating sustained nuclear chain reactions.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Anhydrous cobalt(II) chloride paper is used to detect the chemical presence of liquid water because it changes colour from
questions.Explanation: Anhydrous CoCl2 is blue; upon hydration (CoCl2·6H2O), it turns pink, providing a standard diagnostic test for water.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Which of the following halogens exists as a reddish-brown volatile liquid at room temperature and pressure?
questions.Explanation: At room temperature: F2 (pale yellow gas), Cl2 (greenish-yellow gas), Br2 (reddish-brown liquid), I2 (dark violet crystalline solid).

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: In the laboratory preparation of chlorine gas, concentrated hydrochloric acid is warmed with an oxidizing agent such as
questions.Explanation: MnO2 + 4HCl → MnCl2 + 2H2O + Cl2↑. MnO2 oxidizes Cl⁻ (-1) to elemental chlorine (0).

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Moist chlorine gas bleaches coloured litmus paper and dyes because it acts as an
questions.OptionA: oxidizing agent via the formation of oxochlorate(I) acid (hypochlorous acid, HOCl)
questions.OptionD: reducing agent that adds hydrogen to dyes
questions.Option_a: oxidizing agent via the formation of oxochlorate(I) acid (hypochlorous acid, HOCl)
questions.Option_d: reducing agent that adds hydrogen to dyes
questions.Explanation: Cl2 + H2O ⇌ HCl + HOCl. Unstable HOCl yields nascent oxygen (HOCl → HCl + [O]), which oxidizes and bleaches colored dyes.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Why does dry chlorine gas fail to bleach dry litmus paper?
questions.OptionB: Bleaching action requires water to form hypochlorous acid (HOCl), the active bleaching agent
questions.OptionC: Dry litmus paper absorbs nitrogen instead
questions.OptionD: Atmospheric oxygen is required to ignite the paper
questions.Option_b: Bleaching action requires water to form hypochlorous acid (HOCl), the active bleaching agent
questions.Option_c: Dry litmus paper absorbs nitrogen instead
questions.Option_d: Atmospheric oxygen is required to ignite the paper
questions.Explanation: Without water, no hypochlorous acid (HOCl) forms, so no nascent oxygen is released to bleach the pigment.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: When chlorine gas is bubbled into a colorless solution of potassium bromide (KBr), what observation is made?
questions.OptionA: A white precipitate of potassium forms
questions.OptionB: Dense purple fumes of iodine are evolved
questions.OptionC: The solution turns reddish-brown due to the displacement of bromine by more reactive chlorine
questions.OptionD: No reaction occurs because bromine is more reactive than chlorine
questions.Option_a: A white precipitate of potassium forms
questions.Option_b: Dense purple fumes of iodine are evolved
questions.Option_c: The solution turns reddish-brown due to the displacement of bromine by more reactive chlorine
questions.Option_d: No reaction occurs because bromine is more reactive than chlorine
questions.Explanation: Cl2(g) + 2KBr(aq) → 2KCl(aq) + Br2(aq). Chlorine displaces less electronegative bromide ions, freeing reddish-brown elemental bromine.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Which halogen has the highest oxidizing ability (is the strongest oxidizing agent)?
questions.Explanation: Fluorine has the highest standard reduction potential (+2.87 V), making it the most aggressive oxidizing halogen.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: When chlorine gas reacts with cold, dilute sodium hydroxide solution, the products formed are
questions.OptionA: sodium chloride, sodium oxochlorate(I) (NaClO), and water (bleaching solution)
questions.Option_a: sodium chloride, sodium oxochlorate(I) (NaClO), and water (bleaching solution)
questions.Explanation: Cold dilute alkali: Cl2 + 2NaOH → NaCl + NaClO + H2O. Sodium hypochlorite (NaClO) is household bleach.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: When chlorine gas is bubbled into hot, concentrated sodium hydroxide solution, disproportionation yields
questions.OptionB: sodium chloride (NaCl), sodium chlorate(V) (NaClO3), and water
questions.OptionC: pure sodium metal and chlorine dioxide
questions.Option_b: sodium chloride (NaCl), sodium chlorate(V) (NaClO3), and water
questions.Option_c: pure sodium metal and chlorine dioxide
questions.Explanation: Hot concentrated alkali: 3Cl2 + 6NaOH → 5NaCl + NaClO3 + 3H2O.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Which of the following silver halides is completely insoluble in dilute aqueous ammonia but dissolves in concentrated ammonia?
questions.Explanation: AgCl dissolves in dilute NH3; AgBr dissolves only in concentrated NH3; AgI is insoluble even in concentrated NH3.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Hydrogen chloride gas (HCl) fumes in moist air because it
questions.OptionA: reacts with nitrogen to form ammonium chloride smoke
questions.OptionC: sublimes directly into white snow crystals
questions.OptionD: dissolves readily in atmospheric water vapour to form tiny droplets of hydrochloric acid mist
questions.Option_a: reacts with nitrogen to form ammonium chloride smoke
questions.Option_c: sublimes directly into white snow crystals
questions.Option_d: dissolves readily in atmospheric water vapour to form tiny droplets of hydrochloric acid mist
questions.Explanation: HCl is exceptionally soluble in water (~500 vol HCl in 1 vol H2O); it condenses with atmospheric humidity to form aerosol droplets of acid.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: When hydrogen chloride gas dissolves in non-polar methylbenzene (toluene), the solution
questions.OptionA: does not conduct electricity and does not turn dry blue litmus paper red because it remains molecular without ionizing
questions.OptionB: acts as a strong acid with pH 1.0
questions.Option_a: does not conduct electricity and does not turn dry blue litmus paper red because it remains molecular without ionizing
questions.Option_b: acts as a strong acid with pH 1.0
questions.Explanation: In non-polar solvents, HCl cannot form hydronium ions; it remains un-ionized molecules, displaying no acidic properties.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: The fountain experiment with hydrogen chloride gas demonstrates the gas's
questions.OptionB: extreme solubility in water and acidic nature
questions.Option_b: extreme solubility in water and acidic nature
questions.Explanation: Water entering the flask dissolves HCl so rapidly that a partial vacuum forms, drawing water forcefully into a fountain.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Bleaching powder, widely used for water disinfection and sanitation, is chemically manufactured by passing chlorine gas over
questions.OptionC: dry slaked lime, Ca(OH)2: Ca(OH)2 + Cl2 → CaOCl2 + H2O
questions.Option_c: dry slaked lime, Ca(OH)2: Ca(OH)2 + Cl2 → CaOCl2 + H2O
questions.Explanation: Bleaching powder (calcium hypochlorite / chloride of lime, CaOCl2) is prepared by chlorinating dry Ca(OH)2 at ~40°C.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Tincture of iodine, used as an antiseptic for cleaning skin wounds, consists of
questions.OptionA: pure liquid fluorine in mineral oil
questions.OptionB: chlorine gas dissolved in liquid ammonia
questions.OptionD: iodine dissolved in aqueous potassium iodide and ethanol
questions.Option_a: pure liquid fluorine in mineral oil
questions.Option_b: chlorine gas dissolved in liquid ammonia
questions.Option_d: iodine dissolved in aqueous potassium iodide and ethanol
questions.Explanation: Tincture of iodine is a solution of 2-7% elemental iodine and KI dissolved in a mixture of ethanol and water.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Nitrogen gas (N2) is chemically unreactive (inert) at room temperature because of the
questions.OptionA: extremely high bond dissociation energy of its strong triple covalent bond (:N≡N:)
questions.OptionC: very large atomic radius of the nitrogen atom
questions.Option_a: extremely high bond dissociation energy of its strong triple covalent bond (:N≡N:)
questions.Option_c: very large atomic radius of the nitrogen atom
questions.Explanation: Breaking the N≡N triple bond requires 945 kJ/mol of energy, rendering nitrogen unreactive under ordinary ambient conditions.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: In the laboratory preparation of ammonia gas, an ammonium salt (e.g. NH4Cl) is heated with a strong base like Ca(OH)2. Which drying agent must be used?
questions.Explanation: Ammonia is a basic gas; acidic desiccants (H2SO4, P4O10) react chemically with it, and CaCl2 forms a complex (CaCl2·8NH3). Only basic CaO is suitable.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: What observation confirms the presence of ammonia gas (NH3)?
questions.OptionC: It turns moist red litmus paper blue and gives dense white fumes with concentrated HCl gas
questions.OptionD: It burns with a pop sound
questions.Option_c: It turns moist red litmus paper blue and gives dense white fumes with concentrated HCl gas
questions.Option_d: It burns with a pop sound
questions.Explanation: NH3 is alkaline (turns red litmus blue) and reacts with gaseous HCl to form dense white clouds of ammonium chloride smoke (NH4Cl).

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: The industrial production of nitric acid (HNO3) by the catalytic oxidation of ammonia over platinum-rhodium gauze at 800°C is known as the
questions.Explanation: The Ostwald process oxidizes NH3 to NO over Pt/Rh gauze, which is oxidized to NO2 and absorbed in water to yield HNO3.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: The brown ring test is a confirmatory laboratory test for the presence of which anion?
questions.Explanation: Adding freshly prepared FeSO4 and concentrated H2SO4 to a nitrate solution creates a brown ring of [Fe(H2O)5(NO)]²⁺ at the interface.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Concentrated nitric acid (HNO3) turns yellow upon standing in a glass bottle on the laboratory shelf due to
questions.OptionB: photochemical decomposition into dissolved reddish-brown nitrogen dioxide gas (4HNO3 → 4NO2 + 2H2O + O2)
questions.OptionC: dissolution of silica from the glass bottle
questions.Option_b: photochemical decomposition into dissolved reddish-brown nitrogen dioxide gas (4HNO3 → 4NO2 + 2H2O + O2)
questions.Option_c: dissolution of silica from the glass bottle
questions.Explanation: HNO3 slowly decomposes in sunlight to yield NO2 gas, which dissolves in the acid giving it a yellow or brown appearance.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: The two main crystalline allotropes of sulfur are
questions.Explanation: Sulfur displays crystalline allotropy as octahedral rhombic sulfur (stable below 95.6°C) and needle-shaped monoclinic sulfur (stable above 95.6°C).

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: When sulfur is burned in air or oxygen, it burns with a blue flame to produce a colourless, choking gas named
questions.Explanation: S(s) + O2(g) → SO2(g). SO2 is a pungent, suffocating gas that turns moist blue litmus paper red.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Which of the following gases has the characteristic odor of rotten eggs and precipitates black lead(II) sulfide from lead ethanoate paper?
questions.Explanation: H2S smells foul like rotten eggs and turns filter paper soaked in (CH3COO)2Pb black due to PbS precipitation.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: In the industrial Contact process for manufacturing sulfuric acid, sulfur trioxide (SO3) is absorbed in concentrated H2SO4 rather than water because
questions.OptionA: SO3 is completely insoluble in water
questions.OptionB: direct dissolution in water is violently exothermic and creates an unmanageable mist of acid droplets
questions.OptionC: water oxidizes SO3 into sulfur dioxide
questions.OptionD: concentrated acid freezes the sulfur trioxide
questions.Option_a: SO3 is completely insoluble in water
questions.Option_b: direct dissolution in water is violently exothermic and creates an unmanageable mist of acid droplets
questions.Option_c: water oxidizes SO3 into sulfur dioxide
questions.Option_d: concentrated acid freezes the sulfur trioxide
questions.Explanation: Absorbing SO3 in water produces a corrosive fog; industrially, SO3 is absorbed in 98% H2SO4 to form oleum (H2S2O7), which is safely diluted with water.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Concentrated sulfuric acid acts as a powerful dehydrating agent when it reacts with cane sugar (sucrose, C12H22O11), producing
questions.OptionA: a clear colourless solution of glucose
questions.OptionC: a spongy black mass of carbon (charcoal) and steam
questions.Option_a: a clear colourless solution of glucose
questions.Option_c: a spongy black mass of carbon (charcoal) and steam
questions.Explanation: C12H22O11 → 12C + 11H2O. Concentrated H2SO4 removes hydrogen and oxygen as water, leaving a swollen steaming column of black carbon.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Which reagent is added to an unknown salt solution to confirm the presence of sulphate ions (SO4²⁻) by forming a white precipitate insoluble in dilute acid?
questions.OptionD: Barium chloride solution (BaCl2) acidified with dilute hydrochloric acid
questions.Option_d: Barium chloride solution (BaCl2) acidified with dilute hydrochloric acid
questions.Explanation: Ba²⁺ + SO4²⁻ → BaSO4(s)↓. Barium sulphate is a dense white precipitate insoluble in dilute HCl or HNO3.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: White phosphorus is stored under water because it
questions.OptionA: spontaneously ignites in air at ~30°C (chemiluminescent and pyrophoric)
questions.Option_a: spontaneously ignites in air at ~30°C (chemiluminescent and pyrophoric)
questions.Explanation: White phosphorus (P4) has a very low ignition temperature (~30°C) and oxidizes spontaneously in air; water shields it from contact with atmospheric oxygen.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Superphosphate of lime, an important chemical fertilizer that supplies soluble phosphorus to crops, is manufactured by treating rock phosphate with
questions.Explanation: Insoluble rock phosphate, Ca3(PO4)2, is converted by H2SO4 into a mixture of water-soluble calcium dihydrogen phosphate, Ca(H2PO4)2, and CaSO4.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Metals: Extraction, Properties, and Group Chemistry
questions.Question: Highly reactive metals located at the top of the electrochemical activity series (such as Na, K, Ca, Al) are extracted from their ores exclusively by
questions.OptionA: reduction with carbon (coke) in a blast furnace
questions.OptionB: roasting in a stream of air
questions.OptionC: electrolytic reduction of their molten (fused) salts or oxides
questions.Option_a: reduction with carbon (coke) in a blast furnace
questions.Option_b: roasting in a stream of air
questions.Option_c: electrolytic reduction of their molten (fused) salts or oxides
questions.Explanation: Reactive metals form extremely stable compounds that cannot be reduced by carbon or CO; they require high-energy molten electrolysis.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Metals: Extraction, Properties, and Group Chemistry
questions.Question: Moderately reactive metals (such as iron and zinc) are extracted industrially from their oxide ores by reduction with
questions.OptionB: heating in a stream of pure nitrogen
questions.OptionD: carbon (coke) or carbon monoxide at high temperatures in a blast furnace
questions.Option_b: heating in a stream of pure nitrogen
questions.Option_d: carbon (coke) or carbon monoxide at high temperatures in a blast furnace
questions.Explanation: Metals intermediate in the reactivity series (Zn, Fe, Pb) are economically reduced from oxide ores using carbon/CO in smelting furnaces.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Metals: Extraction, Properties, and Group Chemistry
questions.Question: In the extraction of iron in a blast furnace, what is the main chemical function of limestone (CaCO3)?
questions.OptionA: It acts as a flux, decomposing to CaO which reacts with silica (sand) impurities to form molten slag (CaSiO3)
questions.OptionB: It burns as fuel to heat the furnace
questions.OptionC: It reduces iron(III) oxide directly to iron metal
questions.OptionD: It prevents molten iron from oxidizing
questions.Option_a: It acts as a flux, decomposing to CaO which reacts with silica (sand) impurities to form molten slag (CaSiO3)
questions.Option_b: It burns as fuel to heat the furnace
questions.Option_c: It reduces iron(III) oxide directly to iron metal
questions.Option_d: It prevents molten iron from oxidizing
questions.Explanation: CaCO3 → CaO + CO2. The basic flux CaO combines with acidic gangue (SiO2) to form liquid slag (CaSiO3) that floats on molten iron.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Metals: Extraction, Properties, and Group Chemistry
questions.Question: In the extraction of aluminium by the Hall-Héroult electrolytic process, cryolite (Na3AlF6) is added to molten bauxite (Al2O3) to
questions.OptionA: prevent aluminium from reacting with oxygen
questions.OptionB: lower the melting point of alumina from ~2050°C to ~950°C and improve electrical conductivity
questions.OptionD: bleach the red colour of iron impurities
questions.Option_a: prevent aluminium from reacting with oxygen
questions.Option_b: lower the melting point of alumina from ~2050°C to ~950°C and improve electrical conductivity
questions.Option_d: bleach the red colour of iron impurities
questions.Explanation: Pure Al2O3 melts at >2000°C; dissolving it in molten cryolite lowers operating temperature to ~950°C, drastically cutting energy costs.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Metals: Extraction, Properties, and Group Chemistry
questions.Question: During the electrolysis of alumina in the Hall-Héroult cell, the graphite (carbon) anodes must be replaced periodically because they
questions.OptionA: dissolve completely in the molten aluminium metal
questions.OptionB: melt and coat the bottom of the steel tank
questions.OptionC: react with liberated oxygen gas at high temperature to form carbon dioxide (C + O2 → CO2), burning away
questions.OptionD: become covered in non-conducting sulfur crystals
questions.Option_a: dissolve completely in the molten aluminium metal
questions.Option_b: melt and coat the bottom of the steel tank
questions.Option_c: react with liberated oxygen gas at high temperature to form carbon dioxide (C + O2 → CO2), burning away
questions.Option_d: become covered in non-conducting sulfur crystals
questions.Explanation: Oxygen discharged at the carbon anode oxidizes graphite to CO and CO2 gas at ~950°C, continuously consuming the anode blocks.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Metals: Extraction, Properties, and Group Chemistry
questions.Question: An alloy is defined as a
questions.OptionA: pure metallic element with high electrical resistance
questions.OptionB: corroded layer of metal oxide on an iron pipe
questions.OptionC: solution of a salt in liquid mercury
questions.OptionD: homogeneous mixture of two or more metals (or a metal and a non-metal) to enhance physical properties
questions.Option_a: pure metallic element with high electrical resistance
questions.Option_b: corroded layer of metal oxide on an iron pipe
questions.Option_c: solution of a salt in liquid mercury
questions.Option_d: homogeneous mixture of two or more metals (or a metal and a non-metal) to enhance physical properties
questions.Explanation: Alloys (e.g. steel, brass, bronze) blend elements into metallic solid solutions that exhibit superior strength, hardness, and corrosion resistance.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Metals: Extraction, Properties, and Group Chemistry
questions.Question: Brass is a widely used alloy composed of
questions.Explanation: Brass = Copper (~65%) + Zinc (~35%). Bronze = Copper (~90%) + Tin (~10%).

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Metals: Extraction, Properties, and Group Chemistry
questions.Question: Bronze is an alloy consisting primarily of
questions.Explanation: Bronze consists of copper alloyed with tin (plus minor phosphorus or silicon), used for medals, sculptures, and ship propellers.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Metals: Extraction, Properties, and Group Chemistry
questions.Question: Stainless steel is an alloy of iron containing chromium and nickel, which gives it the valuable property of
questions.OptionC: high resistance to corrosion and rust
questions.Option_c: high resistance to corrosion and rust
questions.Explanation: Chromium (~12-18%) forms an invisible, self-healing passive chromium(III) oxide film that protects stainless steel from rusting.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Metals: Extraction, Properties, and Group Chemistry
questions.Question: Duralumin is an alloy of aluminium containing copper, magnesium, and manganese, valued in the aircraft industry because it is
questions.OptionB: extremely soft and soluble in rainwater
questions.OptionD: lightweight yet possessing high tensile strength
questions.Option_b: extremely soft and soluble in rainwater
questions.Option_d: lightweight yet possessing high tensile strength
questions.Explanation: Duralumin combines the low density of aluminium with the mechanical strength of copper and magnesium, ideal for aeroplane construction.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Metals: Extraction, Properties, and Group Chemistry
questions.Question: An amalgam is a specific type of alloy in which one of the constituent metals is
questions.Explanation: Amalgams are alloys formed by liquid mercury with other metals (e.g. dental silver-tin-mercury amalgam, sodium amalgam Na-Hg).

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Metals: Extraction, Properties, and Group Chemistry
questions.Question: Transition metals (d-block elements) are distinguished by their ability to form
questions.OptionA: only white insoluble salts with zero magnetic properties
questions.OptionB: coloured ions, complex compounds, variable oxidation states, and exhibit catalytic activity
questions.OptionC: noble gas octets in their elemental metallic state
questions.OptionD: gaseous diatomic molecules at room temperature
questions.Option_a: only white insoluble salts with zero magnetic properties
questions.Option_b: coloured ions, complex compounds, variable oxidation states, and exhibit catalytic activity
questions.Option_c: noble gas octets in their elemental metallic state
questions.Option_d: gaseous diatomic molecules at room temperature
questions.Explanation: Partially filled d-orbitals allow d-d electronic transitions (colour), variable valencies (e.g. Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺), and catalytic coordination.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Metals: Extraction, Properties, and Group Chemistry
questions.Question: In flame tests, which characteristic flame colour is imparted by compounds containing sodium ions (Na⁺)?
questions.Explanation: Diagnostic flame emissions: Na⁺ = intense golden yellow; K⁺ = lilac; Ca²⁺ = brick red; Cu²⁺ = blue-green.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Topic: Metals: Extraction, Properties, and Group Chemistry
questions.Question: When sodium hydroxide solution (NaOH) is added dropwise to a solution containing copper(II) ions (Cu²⁺), what is observed?
questions.OptionA: A dirty green precipitate that turns brown
questions.OptionB: A white precipitate that dissolves in excess to give a clear solution
questions.OptionD: A light blue precipitate of Cu(OH)2 forms, which is insoluble in excess NaOH
questions.Option_a: A dirty green precipitate that turns brown
questions.Option_b: A white precipitate that dissolves in excess to give a clear solution
questions.Option_d: A light blue precipitate of Cu(OH)2 forms, which is insoluble in excess NaOH
questions.Explanation: Cu²⁺ + 2OH⁻ → Cu(OH)2(s)↓ (gelatinous light blue precipitate, insoluble in excess aqueous sodium hydroxide).

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Hydrocarbons are organic compounds composed exclusively of
questions.Explanation: By definition, hydrocarbons are binary organic compounds containing solely carbon and hydrogen (e.g. alkanes, alkenes, alkynes, aromatics).

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: The general molecular formula for acyclic saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes or paraffins) is
questions.Explanation: Alkanes have only single C-C bonds and follow the general homologous formula CnH2n+2 (e.g. methane CH4, ethane C2H6).

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: In the laboratory preparation of methane gas, anhydrous sodium ethanoate (CH3COONa) is heated with soda-lime (NaOH + CaO) in a process called
questions.Explanation: CH3COONa + NaOH (soda-lime) → CH4↑ + Na2CO3. Decarboxylation eliminates a carboxyl carbon as carbonate, producing methane.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Alkanes are chemically relatively unreactive under ambient conditions because they contain
questions.OptionD: strong, non-polar carbon-carbon (C-C) and carbon-hydrogen (C-H) sigma bonds
questions.Option_d: strong, non-polar carbon-carbon (C-C) and carbon-hydrogen (C-H) sigma bonds
questions.Explanation: Alkanes (paraffins = 'little affinity') contain stable, non-polar sigma bonds without lone pairs or unsaturation, making them inert to acids and alkalis.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Methane reacts with chlorine gas in diffuse sunlight by which type of chemical mechanism?
questions.Explanation: Photochemical chlorination (CH4 + Cl2 → CH3Cl + HCl) proceeds via a free-radical chain mechanism (initiation, propagation, termination).

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Structural isomerism in organic chemistry is the phenomenon where compounds have the same
questions.OptionA: structural formula but different molecular weights
questions.OptionB: molecular formula but different structural arrangements of atoms

questions.Explanation: Benzene has the molecular formula C6H6, discovered by Michael Faraday in 1825 and possessing a ring structure.

questions.Subject: Chemistry

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Friedel-Crafts alkylation of benzene involves reacting benzene with a haloalkane (e.g. CH3Cl) in the presence of which anhydrous Lewis acid catalyst?
questions.Explanation: C6H6 + CH3Cl (AlCl3) → C6H5CH3 (methylbenzene) + HCl. AlCl3 generates the CH3⁺ carbocation electrophile.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Methylbenzene (toluene, C6H5CH3) is oxidized by refluxing with acidified potassium manganate(VII) (KMnO4) to yield
questions.Explanation: Alkyl side-chains on an aromatic ring are vigorously oxidized by hot acidified KMnO4 down to a single benzoic acid (-COOH) group.

questions.Explanation: Aniline (aminobenzene) is diazotized with nitrous acid to form diazonium salts, which couple with phenols to form synthetic azo dyes.

questions.Explanation: C6H6 + 3H2 (Ni, 180°C) → C6H12 (cyclohexane). Under forcing catalytic conditions, benzene's π-system is saturated.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: In the presence of bright ultraviolet light and the absence of a catalyst, benzene adds three molecules of chlorine to yield the insecticide
questions.Explanation: UV light induces free-radical addition: C6H6 + 3Cl2 (UV) → C6H6Cl6 (1,2,3,4,5,6-hexachlorocyclohexane / BHC).

questions.Explanation: C6H12O6 (zymase in yeast) → 2C2H5OH + 2CO2. Fermentation occurs anaerobically at 25–35°C.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: When a primary alcohol (e.g. ethanol) is oxidized using acidified potassium dichromate(VI), it is oxidized first to an

questions.Option_d: alkanal (aldehyde, e.g. ethanal), and then upon further oxidation to an alkanoic acid (ethanoic acid)
questions.Explanation: 1° alcohols oxidize to aldehydes (-CHO) and subsequently to carboxylic acids (-COOH). Secondary alcohols oxidize to ketones.

questions.Question: Which class of alcohols is resistant to oxidation by acidified potassium dichromate(VI) under normal conditions because it lacks a hydrogen atom on the carbinol carbon?
questions.Explanation: 3° alcohols lack a C-H bond on the carbon bearing the -OH group; oxidizing them requires breaking C-C bonds under destructive forcing conditions.

questions.Question: Carboxylic acids (alkanoic acids) possess which characteristic functional group?
questions.Explanation: Carboxylic acids have the -COOH group (carbonyl C=O combined with hydroxyl -OH) with general formula CnH2n+1COOH.

questions.Explanation: In dilute aqueous solution, only ~1% of ethanoic acid molecules dissociate, behaving as a typical weak organic acid.

questions.Explanation: Carboxylic acid + Alcohol (conc. H2SO4 catalyst, reflux) ⇌ Ester + Water. The concentrated acid acts as catalyst and dehydrating agent.

questions.Explanation: Saponification: Fat/Oil + 3NaOH → Glycerol (propane-1,2,3-triol) + 3 Sodium salts of fatty acids (Soap).

questions.Explanation: Carbohydrates ('hydrates of carbon') follow the empirical formula Cx(H2O)y, as in glucose (C6H12O6) and sucrose (C12H22O11).

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Which of the following carbohydrates is a simple hexose monosaccharide that serves as the primary cellular respiratory substrate?
questions.Explanation: Glucose is a 6-carbon monosaccharide (aldohexose) directly oxidized during cellular glycolysis and respiration to yield ATP.

questions.Question: Sucrose (table sugar, C12H22O11) is a disaccharide formed by the condensation of which two monosaccharide units?
questions.Explanation: Sucrose consists of an α-D-glucopyranosyl unit linked to a β-D-fructofuranosyl unit via an α,β-1,2-glycosidic bond.

questions.Explanation: Condensation of adipic acid and hexamethylenediamine eliminates water to form polyamide chains with amide links (-CO-NH-), forming Nylon-6,6.

questions.Option_c: soften when heated and can be remoulded and recycled repeatedly

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Vulcanization of natural rubber involves heating raw rubber with sulfur to

questions.Question: Petroleum (crude oil) is a complex naturally occurring mixture consisting predominantly of
questions.Explanation: Crude oil is a fossil fuel formed from ancient marine organic matter, comprising thousands of paraffinic, naphthenic, and aromatic hydrocarbons.

questions.OptionB: fractional distillation in a fractionating column
questions.Option_b: fractional distillation in a fractionating column
questions.Explanation: Fractional distillation separates crude oil into fractions (refinery gas, petrol, kerosene, diesel, lubricating oil, bitumen) by vaporization and condensation.

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: Acid rain is caused primarily by atmospheric emissions of which two industrial gaseous pollutants?
questions.Explanation: Combustion of sulfur-containing fossil fuels and vehicle engines releases SO2 and NO2, which react with rainwater to form H2SO4 and HNO3 (pH < 5.0).

questions.Subject: Chemistry
questions.Question: The Greenhouse Effect and global warming are driven primarily by the buildup of which gas released from the combustion of fossil fuels?
questions.Explanation: CO2 absorbs and re-emits outgoing terrestrial infrared radiation, trapping thermal energy in the troposphere and warming the global climate.
